title.narrative: CO- Response to internal displacement in

description.narrative:
An ongoing military offensive against IS in the Bari region and clan conflicts in Erigavo, Sanaag region, are causing daily casualties and displacement, a situation anticipated to persist in the coming weeks.The number of people displaced for safety and protection is steadily increasing, and the likelihood of their immediate return to areas of origin remains minimal. Concurrently, the ongoingmilitary campaign against IS in Bari is likely to expand geographically, potentially causing further displacementfrom areas such asTasjiic in Bossaso district.
This crisis remains largely unattended. Host communities are entering the annual dry season, during which resources—especially water and food—are at critically low levels, limiting their ability to support displaced populations. The displaced population numbers are already significantly high (119,000 people due to military offensive and 40,000 due to clan conflict), and their humanitarian needs are multi-sector. Many displaced households are particularlyvulnerable, including separated families and women-headed households, urgently requiring targeted assistance.
The Puntland Government has launched a military operation bolstered by U.S. airstrikes against IS militants in the Bari region or Puntland. As of February 2025, Erigavo district in Sanaag region continues to experience significant clan-based conflict, predominantly between the Warsangeli and Habar Jeclo clans. Triggered bypolitical rivalries, resource disputes, and territorial claims, violence notably escalated, causing widespread displacement of approximately 43,000 people (22,680 women and 19,320 men). Food security conditions for displaced and vulnerable host households have deteriorated sharply. In Erigavo, WASH conditions are dire in both displacement contexts. In Erigavo, 43% of sites lack access to safewater, while 79% face severe water shortages, resulting in widespread open defecation (55%) and high risk of acute water diarrhea/cholera outbreaks due to overcrowding (76%) and poor sanitation (57%) in sites. In Bari, the situation is equally critical, with only25% having access to safe drinking water, forcing 81% of displaced households to use unsafe sources, and 75% practicing open defecation. Significant protection issues are evidentin both regions along with Shelter conditions that are critical in both displacement contexts
Oxfam Somalia program aims to support approximately 846 displaced individuals representing the most vulnerable people fromthe displaced population who will be selected via multi-purpose cash injection to address the immediate food needs of food insecureHHs. The response will prioritize 2 displacement sites hosting 29,976 IDPs affected by the military offensive in Bari and 4 sites accommodating approximately10,500 IDPs displaced by the Erigavo conflict. These locations will be accessible from Oxfam’s Garowe office in Puntland and have been identified as priority areas for multipurpose cash transfer humanitarian assistance
Oxfam Somalia program has secured 290,000 USD from start network on 26th February which mainly focuses on cash injection on top of WASH and Protection. Oxfam will now complement SN project to this project and collectively reach additional 2400 people on MPCA making the total numberofcash beneficiaries to 6,810 people which represents 16% coverage of our target locations.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
